Working in collaboration with an illuminate from the Astral Ward, we've begun research on the magically dense mirrors that are strewn throughout the city ruins. Upon inspection, this illuminate has informed me that these mirrors are tethered together via a type of magic called shadowcraft. Prior records on shadowcraft are brief and limited to observations of mursaat cloaking abilities.  
  
In practice, the mirrors are portals, or gateways, and are connected to a small dimension that exists between Tyria and the Mists. When someone travels through one of these mirrors, their essence is temporarily distorted, and they are able to quickly jump from one mirror to another.

strings.en:
My fellow seers,  
  
The time has come for us to abandon this place, lest it fall into the hands of the shadow stalkers. While this decision was not made lightly, there are aspects of our actions that we must now make haste to address.  
  
This tablet, which has been ensorcelled to be readable only by the trusted few who have attained their initiate level of our ascension ritual, must bear the burden of one of our people's most cherished secrets: the path that leads to the Navarium Core.  
  
For eons, it was my humble charge to lead those of us who are chosen to the hidden path through the Spire of Exaltation. However, I have now been tasked with a greater purpose, and this requires me to leave this tablet in my stead. 
  
I, and five of my siblings, are to become guardians of this place. Avatars of the All Seer, we will defend our blessed garden, and the many secrets it contains, for all eternity. I shall bear this responsibility with honor, and I pray that our watch will endure through the ages.  
  
If you seek the path I once illuminated, you must follow the steps of one of the other high stewards, for only they can reveal the way.  
  
May the All Seer watch and guide us,  
Gardesano

While much has been made of the seers' connection to magic, the theory that they possessed a once-great civilization that has since been lost appears to be entirely baseless. While the proponents are quick to point out the destructive capabilities of the mursaat for explaining the lack of surviving architecture, they miss the more obvious explanation: the seers never built them in the first place. In all likelihood, they were a primarily nomadic people, possibly early agrarian in some places, but there just exists very little evidence to suggest more than that.  
  
Supporters of this idea also frequently reference the oft-repeated legends of the seers and their influence in the ancient war against the Elder Dragons. What they fail to recognize is that this fits in perfectly with one of the most common archetypal myths: the ancient, powerful civilization, who once ruled over the world, but then fell and left it to us to take over. It's entirely possible that the seers played a role in the conflict, but that doesn't mean these myths can be taken as literal truth.  
  
If this field of study is going to experience any success, we need to avoid expending our efforts searching for evidence we're unlikely to ever find. While not technically impossible, the likelihood of discovering a massive, lost seer structure is indistinguishable from zero. It would be more sensible for us to focus our efforts on better understanding what we've already uncovered.

I was just awoken by screams and what sounded like the low reverberations of beating wings.  
  
I've closely watched the goings-on in what appears to be an amphitheater or coliseum below. I can only assume it has seen better times. Or at least more significant times. I recall Grink chittering about it being a place of historical infamy, but I'm unable to verify that claim.  
  
A few Kryptis come and go, but for the most part it seems unoccupied. Until now. I do not want to meet whatever creature is associated with those reverberations. It's easy to believe this was once a place of tragedy. Perhaps one day this great arena can be a venue for glorious happenings if Lady Peitha succeeds. I hope I live to see it.  
  
For now, I must find safer refuge, so I will work my way past this decrepit arena and continue north.  

—Operative Selly
